caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, 2:30 AM. He's 81, anxious, can't sleep. His as-needed order: hydrOXYzine 25 mg by mouth.

❌ 3 mistakes, 3 error types
1️⃣ Missed keyword: read "hydr..." and grabbed hydrALAZINE
2️⃣ Habit over standard: the scanner said "wrong drug", and the nurse overrode it
3️⃣ Wrong priority: "I feel dizzy", and the med pass came first
➡️ 3:45 AM: BP (blood pressure) 84/48, dizzy and confused. Rapid response.

🔤 Hydralazine vs hydroxyzine (READ EVERY LETTER)
• hydrALAZINE: relaxes the arteries and lowers blood pressure
• hydrOXYzine: an antihistamine for anxiety and itching
• Look-alike, sound-alike names: tall-man letters show the difference

✅ The right move
• Read the whole name, every letter
• Scan every dose. A scanner alert means stop and check
• Match the drug to the reason it's ordered
• Dizzy after a dose? Check BP, stay with him, call

🧠 One letter apart. Read every letter.

Hydralazine: arterial vasodilator; hypotension with reflex tachycardia

Story: hydralazine 25 mg by mouth given in error to an 81-year-old not on it (usual start is 10 mg four times a day); BP 84/48, heart rate 112, dizzy and confused about 70 minutes later (onset about 45 min, peak about 2 h). Softened from 72/40 after Vera's check. Realistic?
Hydroxyzine in an 81-year-old is itself on the Beers list (anticholinergic). Not raised in the Reel to keep one lesson; diphenhydramine Beers Reel posted Nov 23. OK?
Labetalol (HTN emergency, Nov 23) is a different drug. OK under the 30-day rule?
